references.text: The same chapter describes impurity rules for anyone who touches the bed or objects that the person with a discharge has sat on, and requires the same cleansing process of washing clothes and bathing.
Repeats the principle that anyone who touches something that was under the person with a discharge becomes unclean until evening and must wash their clothes.
The same cleansing regulation involving washing clothes and being unclean until evening is found in connection with carrying carcasses of unclean animals.
A parallel rule about washing clothes and being unclean until evening after contact with unclean things.
The same cleansing ritual of washing clothes, bathing in water, and being unclean until evening applies to anyone who eats animals that died naturally.
A similar purity regulation where the one who gathers the ashes from the red heifer must wash their clothes and be unclean until evening.
The same principle of being unclean until evening and transmitting impurity through touching unclean objects.
A priest who touches something unclean becomes unclean until evening, the same timeframe for impurity as in Leviticus 15:6.
